title: Stocks could fall 20% as Huang fails to revive AI boom, research firm warns
excerpt: Capital Economics said it saw the S&P 500 dropping as much as 20% next year as momentum in the AI trade slows.
content_html:
Jensen Huang’s return won’t stave off a looming 20% drop in stocks, a research firm warns

By Jennifer Sor

You're currently following this author! Click to unsubscribe from email alerts.

2026-11-27T10:40:02.474Z

Jensen Huang momentarily revived the AI rally last week, but even the stunning comeback one of the world's most powerful tech moguls can't stop more pain coming for stocks.

That sentiment was already on display as markets sold off sharply on Tuesday and Wednesday, but Capital Economics is warning of a deeper drawdown as the AI trade falters.

Capital Economics said it was sticking to its call for the S&P 500 to drop as much as 20% over the next six to twelve months, pointing to several factors that suggested the AI trade will continue to stumble.

The firm sees the S&P 500 ending 2027 at 6,500, implying an 8% drop in the index.

The coming drop in stocks is unlikely to tip the US economy into a recession, Jonas Goltermann, chief markets economist at the firm, wrote in a note.

"This is the main reason that we 'only' have a roughly 20% fall in our forecast, rather than the much larger fall which followed the dotcom bust," he wrote of the larger fallout in the AI trade.

Investors were hopeful that Huang's return might me Nvidia will keep striking new AI deals, which have come under focus as the market frets about the pace of capex spending and a possible slowdown in data center construction.

But expectations for continued growth in the AI trade look misguided, Goltermann said, pointing to four issues that suggest momentum in the industry is about to slow:

  1. AI investment could pull back & earnings could disappoint. Raising new capital in the industry now looks "increasingly challenging" for smaller firms on shakier financial footing, Goltermann said. Borrowing costs have climbed in the past year on AI debt, thanks to factors like the larger supply of available debt and a concurrent rise in bond yields.

    "That means that a self-reinforcing negative cycle could easily take hold. We expect capex to slow and earnings to disappoint lofty expectations over the coming months," he said.

  2. AI sentiment could be hit by regulators. "Many federal and state-level legislative and judicial officials appear to take a dimmer view of recent events, and of the AI roll out more broadly. That will probably still hamper the AI boom and sentiment," Goltermann said.
  3. The Fed is expected to hike rates, another headwind to equity prices. After Wednesday's hot PCE data, markets are pricing in a 94% chance rates will be at least 25 basis points next month.

    "Historically, the Fed has had a tendency to 'hike until something breaks'. At the current juncture, the AI boom appears quite breakable," Goltermann said.

  4. Possible impact on economic growth. While the US looks poised to avoid a recession, lower stock prices are likely to hit consumers due to the wealth effect, the phenomenon where people spend more as stocks rise and their net worth increases. Still, the US growth outlook has become "ever more dependent on the AI boom," Capital Economics said.

"Our assessment is that the more pessimistic view on the AI equity boom which we have set out since early summer is playing out faster than we had expected. We doubt the S&P 500 will regain its early October peak any time soon," Goltermann added.

Chatter about the potential collapse of the AI trade has grown louder in recent months as the tech sell-off has picked up steam. Though the AI sector has regained some of its footing, tech stocks remain deep in correction territory, with the Nasdaq 100 down 16% from its latest peak.
